passage: "Look what you've done! Every single morning!" Zeenat heard her own voice bounce off the kitchen tiles. The milk was spreading across the table, the school bus was due in ten minutes, and five-year-old Dilnaz stood frozen with her lip trembling. Zeenat's chest went hot with guilt at once. She stepped to the sink, ran the tap and took three slow breaths. Then she came back and crouched down. "Mummy shouted, and I'm sorry. Spilled milk is not a big problem. I was rushing and I got cross." Dilnaz sniffed. "Let's wipe it together," Zeenat said, handing her a cloth. They made the bus with a minute to spare, and Dilnaz waved from the window.

qa.a: Dilnaz spilled the milk on the table.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling right after she snapped?
qa.a: She felt hot guilt straight away, on top of stress about the bus, so she stopped at the sink to breathe.

qa.q: What did Zeenat do that teaches Dilnaz more than never getting angry would?
qa.a: She calmed herself, apologised, named her own mistake and cleaned up together, showing that anger can be mended.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz have felt when her mother shouted, and afterwards?
qa.a: Dilnaz was probably scared and ashamed, as her frozen stance and trembling lip suggest, and then relieved when her mother came back kind. 🙂

grounding: Shows a parent snapping at her child, feeling guilty, then apologising and regulating herself.

passage:
"Hemant! I told you not to carry the juice to the sofa!" Deepika shouted.

Hemant, five, froze with the empty cup. Orange juice was spreading across the cushion.

"Why can't you ever listen?" she said, even louder.

His eyes filled. He dropped the cup and ran to his room.

Deepika stood there, breathing hard. She had been up at five with a work deadline. She sat on the floor for a minute and counted her breaths. Then she knocked on his door.

"Can I come in?"

"No."

"Okay. I'll sit here." She sat outside. "Hemant, I shouted. That was not okay. I was tired and cross, and I took it out on you. I'm sorry."

The door opened a crack. "You were really loud."

"I was. Next time I'm cross, I'll stop and take three breaths first. Will you help me remember?"

He nodded. "And I'll carry juice to the table."

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling as she sat on the floor counting her breaths?
qa.a: Deepika felt guilty and exhausted after shouting, and was trying to calm her own anger.

qa.q: What did Deepika's apology teach Hemant?
qa.a: It modelled owning a mistake, naming feelings and a plan to calm down, which teaches more than pretending to be perfect.

qa.q: What was it like for Hemant when his mother shouted?
qa.a: Hemant felt scared and hurt; his eyes filled and he ran to his room.

grounding: Shows a young mother snapping at her child, feeling guilty, and modelling apology and self-regulation.

passage:
This morning I snapped at Madhuri. I'm writing it down so I remember what I did afterwards, not only the snapping.

We were late. Madhuri, who is four, wanted to wear her rain boots on a sunny day and cried when I said no. I said, "Amala has no time for this!" and pulled the boots off her feet. She went completely quiet in the auto. That silence was worse than crying.

All day at the office I felt heavy. I kept thinking I'm the kind of mother I promised I'd never be.

At bedtime I sat on her bed. "Madhuri, this morning Amala was angry and pulled your boots off. I'm sorry. Next time I'm rushing, I'll tell you I'm feeling hurried and we'll decide together."

She thought about it. "Can I wear them tomorrow?"

"If it's not muddy, yes."

She hugged my arm. I'm Dolma, I'm twenty-five, and I'm still learning.

qa.q: What was Dolma feeling during the day at the office?
qa.a: Dolma felt heavy with guilt and shame, fearing being the kind of mother promised never to be.

qa.q: What did Dolma model for Madhuri at bedtime?
qa.a: Dolma named the anger, apologised and offered a plan for next time, showing how to repair after losing patience.

qa.q: What was the ride in the auto like for Madhuri?
qa.a: Madhuri was so hurt and upset that she went completely quiet, which worried Dolma more than crying.

grounding: Shows a young mother who snaps at her child, feels guilty, and models apology and self-regulation.
